applicability_boundary.prohibited_claim: Performance on these datasets is not evidence of generalization across contact-resistance values.
applicability_boundary.statement: P1h, P1i, and V6 random-block cannot identify or learn response variation caused by finite interface thermal contact resistance because every generated case fixes R_contact=0.

evidence.interpretation: P1h changes support only and inherits the P1g physical cases unchanged.
The perfect-contact keyword is the R_contact=0 limit.
evidence.solver_semantics: Neighbor-face conductance uses the harmonic conductivity only; no finite interface resistance term is present.

continuous_broad_coverage.conclusion: continuous broad coverage is supported across the frozen observed ranges; strict uniformity is not supported and is not claimed

methodology.joint_physical_occupancy: 6x6 cells in frozen config ranges using sampling-native linear/log10 transforms; derived quantities use frozen observed bounds.
methodology.joint_rank_occupancy: 6x6 cells after marginal empirical-rank transforms, isolating joint dependence from marginal skew.
methodology.split_use: train/valid_iid/test_iid are compared descriptively; test_iid does not set thresholds, alter split assignment, or authorize selection.
methodology.uniform_reference: For each scalar metric, values are min-max normalized over the frozen observed support and compared with Uniform(0,1). KS and Wasserstein are diagnostics, not acceptance tests.

known_boundaries: power and top_h are deliberately coupled; the high-power/low-top-h corner is absent
finite contact-resistance response cannot be learned
test_iid was read only for this preregistered descriptive split audit and did not modify rules
training_authorization.scope: Training authorization is limited to the frozen formal1024_v1 coupled input distribution. It is not an OOD or strict-uniform claim.
